schema_authority_boundary.reason: v3.1 resolves the ProjectionAST/Gate0/DP execution-order conflict. It does not change the A1 persisted envelope or domain-field layout. The schema identifier therefore remains 3.0 while the ReleaseLedger locks the v3.1 authority SHA; this avoids a cosmetic schema bump that would make downstream version checks drift without a layout migration.

root_causes: FactAssembler sorted same-span drafts only by span, semantic, and case-folded statement. Distinct typed facts such as two characters in one sentence could therefore retain provider return order, changing local ordinals, IDs, handles, and FactRegistry bytes.
Case-folding fact statements could merge distinct source-supported semantics such as 'US' and 'us', allowing a lossy model-facing normalization to erase a fact.
Fact identity omitted source_kind, so otherwise identical SCRIPT and CONTINUITY facts could mint the same persistent ID and model-selection handle.
canonical_sha256 preserved CRLF/CR in structured text, contrary to the frozen cross-platform canonical-text rule and capable of producing checkout-dependent hashes.
The legacy checkpoint observation retained an absolute host path as its locator, which was non-canonical and unsafe to carry into later pipeline data.
repair: FactAssembler now orders by source span plus the complete typed draft identity and preserves case/internal whitespace semantics. The same semantic input set is permutation-invariant before IDs are minted.
source_kind participates in the local fact identity; ScriptFact is registered as an envelope-valid canonical payload type.
Draft-facing fact text is NFC-normalized and edge-trimmed locally before source support, grouping, hashing, or persistence; no raw tick field or source-span-to-time conversion was introduced.
Structured canonical hashes normalize CRLF/CR to LF. binary_sha256 explicitly hashes bytes without normalization, preserving media/binary evidence semantics.
The read-only legacy adapter now exposes only a stable legacy-checkpoint filename locator and still cannot mint vNext IDs, handles, or artifacts.
